subject: Datagrid multi-region Dedicated: capacity mix, DR options, and commit pricing
messages:
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@datagrid.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@datagrid.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Multi-region Dedicated quote request (US + EU) — RFP attached

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We pulled together a brief RFP for our infra team (attached). TL;DR: we want a committed Dedicated deployment that spans US (primary) + EU (replicated/DR) with deterministic throughput guarantees for our inference endpoints. High-level asks: 

- Steady-state throughput: equivalent of ~800k tokens/day (peak ~2x), roughly 50 concurrent user inference sessions.
- Primary region (us-west): target 8 GPU-equivalents (A100 class) serving model-v2 pinned; secondary (eu-west): warm-standby with 4 GPU-equivalents for replication and fast failover.
- Cross-region routing: prefer regional routing for latency, but automatic failover to EU pool if US capacity is impaired.
- SLA: 99.95% region-level availability; credits if we miss p99 latency guarantees.
- Commercial: looking at a 12-month committed spend, want pricing + discount tiers and any packaging options (active-active vs active-standby, snapshot/kv-cache warmup strategies).

Can you send a proposal and ballpark numbers (monthly committed cost + expected overage rates) so we can review with procurement? We attached the RFP as Datagrid_RFP_Q2.pdf.

Thanks,
Ben Turner
Head of Platform, DataGrid
ben.turner@datagrid.ai


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@datagrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated quote request (US + EU) — RFP attached

Ben — great to see the RFP, thanks. Attaching a short proposal (proposal-datagrid-q2.pdf) but wanted to call out the packaging and trade-offs up front so your infra and procurement teams can digest quickly. High level options we recommend: 

1) Active-Standby (cost-efficient, fast failover)
   - Primary pool: 8 dedicated GPU-equivalents (A100 class), pinned to model-v2.
   - Secondary pool (warm): 4 GPU-equivalents, KV-cache snapshots + async replication.
   - Failover: automated routing switch within 30–90s; cold-cache warmup ~60–120s depending on working set.
   - Pricing: $145,000/mo committed (12m) for the reserved pools above + 12% discount on token-based overage.

2) Active-Active (higher availability, lower failover latency)
   - Primary & secondary both sized to handle ~60% of peak load each (8 + 6 equiv).
   - Continuous cross-region replication of KV caches to reduce warmup.
   - Pricing: $210,000/mo committed (12m) with 18% committed discount; includes free cross-region snapshot replication (network egress pass-through).

Other notes:
- Throughput SLOs: we can include a p99 token latency SLO tied to each pool at the committed size; we offer service credits on a sliding scale for p99 misses.
- Routing: policy-based routing (latency preferred; failover to compatible model variant if exact model version not pinned). We can support model pinning across regions for the same version.
- Commit terms: 12m vs 24m moves discounts from ~12% to ~20% depending on total committed spend and add-on services (extended observability retention, private VPC connectors).

I've copied Ben Carter (Sales) to confirm commercial flexibility; he'll loop in finance for margin checks. If this looks reasonable I can produce a formal quote and add a DocuSign link.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0134

Attachment: proposal-datagrid-q2.pdf (15 pages)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Datagrid multi-region Dedicated: capacity mix, DR options, and commit pricing

Soojin — forwarding the ask. Quick internal notes: 
- Finance (Laura) — can we carve the 12m committed numbers to give procurement some play? Client asked for negotiation on % discount versus absolute monthly commit.
- Margin check: Active-Standby at $145k/mo — target margin band ok? If we trim to $130k to land the deal, what impact on promo credits / onboarding credits?
- Cross-region egress: double-check that free replication only applies with our cross-region pass-through; otherwise we need to include an egress line item.

Laura — any quick guidance so we can get a firm quote out early next week.

—Ben
From: Ben Turner <ben.turner@datagrid.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 16:40:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated: quick clarifications before quote

Thanks Soojin and Ben — this looks promising. A couple clarifications from procurement before we sign off to your commercial team: 

- Can you confirm whether the $145k/mo Active-Standby assumes any free warm-cache snapshots or if we should budget ~1–2 hours of miss penalty on cold-start for the first request after failover? We need a numeric expectation.
- For active-active, you mentioned network egress pass-through — please confirm if that is included or capped at a threshold (we have high cross-region traffic during model sync windows).
- Discount flexibility: if we move to a 24-month commit, what final pricing can you offer? We are targeting < $120k/mo effective committed cost (net of credits).
- SLA: can we add a p99 latency SLA for the primary region in the Appendix and tie credits to measurable thresholds (we use Datadog; can instrument p99 easily).

If you can add these to the formal quote and throw in a 30-day onboarding credit for warm-cache pre-warming, we can move to procurement signatures quickly.

Best,
Ben

On Thu, Apr 02, 2026 at 09:12 Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> [Original message included above]
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Turner <ben.turner@datagrid.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region Dedicated: quick clarifications before quote

Ben — thanks, good questions. Answering inline and committing next steps below.

- Warm-cache snapshots / cold-start: Active-Standby option includes weekly automated KV snapshot replication and one dedicated warm-cache pre-warm window during onboarding (30–60 minutes). In a full failover event we expect an additional cold-warm penalty of ~45–90s to reach >90% hit-rate on working set (best-effort; depends on working set size). We'll include a quantitative estimate in Appendix B of the formal quote.

- Cross-region egress: for the Active-Active SKU we include up to 20TB/mo cross-region replication traffic at no additional charge; above that we pass through egress at cost + 10% handling fee (we'll show a sample run-rate table). For Active-Standby we include up to 5TB/month of snapshot replication.

- 24-month pricing: we can move to $118,000/mo effective for an Active-Standby footprint with a 24-month commit (DG-2026-042-24M). That assumes standard onboarding credits (30 days) and a one-time professional services fee if you want deeper cache-warm strategies.

- SLA & p99 latency: happy to include a primary-region p99 latency SLA in the Appendix with measurable Datadog-based thresholds and a tiered credit schedule. We'll align on monitoring metrics and an SLO report cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) We issue a formal, itemized quote (includes Appendix A: SLOs; Appendix B: cache warmup expectations; Appendix C: network / egress assumptions).
2) Ben Carter will confirm final discount authorization and routing on the DocuSign.
3) We'll provision a 30-day onboarding credit window to accelerate cache warmup once the DocuSign is signed.

I'll draft the formal quote and send a DocuSign link by COB Mon (12 Apr) unless you ask for an earlier timeline.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a signature.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
